newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila banks sidelined in secondary T-bill market.
newsitem.headline: Manila banks sidelined in secondary T-bill market.

text.p: Philippine banks were sidelined in the secondary Treasury bills market on Friday as they took a cautious stance on their liquidity positions, traders said.
"There's the possibility of tightness because of the additional reserve requirements," a trader said.
The central bank said on Wednesday it was raising the liquidity reserve to four percent from three percent in order to siphon money that would have gone to peso speculation.
"We'll probably wait and see until the peso stabilises," a second dealer said.
Traders said the market had more sellers because banks wanted to remain liquid.
A Reuters poll of eight financial institutions gave offers of 13.40/15.50 percent for the three-month bills; 13.875/15.34 percent for the six months; and 14.25/15 percent for the one-year bills.
The average interbank call loan rate was steady at 20.0625 percent, with 25 lenders and 18 borrowers.
Volume was lower at 14.91 billion pesos from 16.84 billion pesos. -- Lilian Karunungan (63 2) 841-8937
